original_question: Does every closed manifold of dimension at least 2 admit either a Riemannian metric or a Finsler metric whose geodesic flow is ergodic?
target_in_paper: Section 8.1's opening, unnumbered problem: "Does every closed manifold (with dimension ≥ 2) admit a metric (Riemannian or Finsler) with ergodic geodesic flow?" This is the sentence immediately before the narrower positive-curvature Question 8.1.1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
correct_elements: Your draft matches the paper on the main quantifier (every closed manifold), the dimension threshold (at least 2), the allowed metric classes (Riemannian or Finsler), and the target property (ergodicity of the geodesic flow). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
missing_details: The paper works under the standing convention that M is connected, so the target problem is about closed connected manifolds. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
To make the question stand-alone, one should name the flow as the geodesic flow g_t on the unit tangent bundle SM associated with the chosen metric. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))

"Ergodic" should be made measure-theoretic: the natural intended measure is the Liouville measure on SM; elsewhere in the paper, when ergodicity of geodesic flow is stated explicitly, this is the measure used. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))

The target is the general existence problem in Section 8.1, not the immediately following narrower question imposing everywhere positive sectional curvature. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
refined_question: Let M be a closed connected manifold with dim M ≥ 2. Does there exist on M a Riemannian metric or a Finsler metric such that the associated geodesic flow g_t on the corresponding unit tangent bundle SM is ergodic with respect to the natural Liouville measure? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
justification: The draft is already very close, but the exact target in the paper is the unnumbered opening problem of Section 8.1, not Question 8.1.1, which adds the extra hypothesis of everywhere positive sectional curvature. Section 1 supplies the hidden notation and scope: M is a connected manifold, SM is the unit tangent bundle, and g_t is the geodesic flow. Since ergodicity in the paper's explicit nearby usage is with respect to the Liouville measure, adding that measure makes the question fully stand-alone without broadening it beyond the paper's intent. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
